notes.note: Verses 121-128 are the stanza ayin, 129-136 the stanza pe; every verse in a stanza begins with that letter. The packet's KJV text carries the letter-heading (ע AIN, פ PE) at 121 and 129 only; these are not part of the Hebrew verse and I have ignored them.

Window carries the dalet stanza (vv. 25-32) and the first four verses of the he stanza (vv. 33-36). The KJV prints the Hebrew letter names DALETH and HE as headings in the verse text, and the ASV prints 'HE' at the end of v. 32 where it belongs to v. 33. The Hebrew verses carry no letter name; I ignored these in the layers and mentioned it in v. 25 and v. 33. The acrostic itself is real: all eight verses of the dalet stanza begin with ד, all of the he stanza with ה.

[verse.en:PS.119.5] אַחֲלַי occurs here and in 2 Kgs 5:3. Rashi, Radak, Meiri and Metzudat Zion take it as a noun, 'my prayer/plea', tied to the root יחל; the five English versions all read an optative 'would that'. I follow the optative in the literal layer and give the commentators' reading in the note.

[verse.en:PS.119.8] Whether עד מאד belongs to 'I will keep' (Radak, Metzudat David, Meiri) or to 'do not forsake me' (Ibn Ezra, KJV and the other English versions) is disputed. I kept it with the plea, as the English versions do, and did not claim a cantillation argument I cannot source.

[verse.en:PS.119.17] KJV and Webster print the Gimel heading before this verse; the Hebrew text carries no heading in the verse, and the Gimel section is v17-24, each line opening with gimel. Translated the Hebrew as it stands.

[verse.en:PS.119.18] גַּל here is from גלה 'uncover' (H1540); in v22 the identical form גַּל is from גלל 'roll away' (H1556). STEPBible has both right. Meiri on v22 notes the pausal-looking vowel and the debate between the two roots; I follow Rashi and the majority: גלל.

[verse.en:PS.119.21] The five English versions split: KJV/ASV/Webster read 'cursed' as describing the arrogant; BBE makes it a separate clause. I keep אֲרוּרִים as adjectival, parallel to זֵדִים, and the participle הַשֹּׁגִים as a further description. Radak takes גערת as a past form with future sense; I render the perfect plainly and note the debate.
Названия букв (Далет, Хе) в русском тексте не печатаются; в комментарии они названы по английскому, как «далет» и «хе».
